**PR #5277 is up — and its ablation corrects a prediction I put in the dispatch order.**

I wrote: *"delete `user: 'field:user'` from `field-type-alias.ts`, predict that the form half now goes red (it should — that is the whole fix) **alongside the cell half**."*

That last clause is wrong. The dev predicted the opposite before running, from reading the code, and observed it:

```
x maps "user" to a dedicated form widget (not field:text)
  AssertionError: expected 'field:text' not to be 'field:text'
Tests  1 failed | 87 passed (88)
```

**Only the form half went red.** The cell half stayed green, because `getCellRenderer('user')` resolves through an **independent** registration — `registerFieldRenderer('user', UserCellRenderer)` in `index.tsx` plus a literal map entry — which never consults `field-type-alias.ts`'s `typeMap` at all.

Worth being precise about why I was wrong, because the card had it right and I garbled it: the card says *"删 `registerFieldRenderer('user'|'owner', UserCellRenderer)` 会红,删对应的表单别名不会红"* — i.e. the two halves have **independent resolution paths**, and which mutation you make decides which half reddens. Deleting the *alias* was only ever going to touch the form half. I collapsed two different mutations into one expected outcome.

This also sharpens what the card is actually about. The asymmetry is not "one list is missing an entry" — it is that **the two halves of one guard resolve through two unrelated mechanisms**, so a single list omission makes the guard blind in exactly one direction with no signal. The fix closes that, and the ablation is what proves it rather than merely asserting it.

The `owner` boundary was held: left out of `FORM_WIDGET_TYPES`, tombstone at `field-type-alias.ts:74-81` untouched, and the full `packages/fields` suite (107 files / 1802 tests) run so `owner-retired.test.tsx` was exercised alongside the change rather than assumed unaffected.
